disease_label_per_paper: Diabetic foot infection caused by Burkholderia cepacia complex

demographics.source_text_value: 42-year-old male patient with type-2 diabetes mellitus

presentation_summary: 42-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and small-fiber diabetic neuropathy suffered an unrecognized plantar puncture injury from glass while playing soccer in a muddy field containing rubbish and dog feces.
After glass removal, he returned two days later with intense pain, erythema, and swelling at the plantar left foot and received oral amoxicillin/clavulanate plus ciprofloxacin without improvement.
He was hospitalized after treatment failure; infection was PEDIS grade 3, extending beyond subcutaneous tissue or with erythema exceeding 2 cm, but no systemic signs were noted.

Admission vitals were BP 130/80 mmHg, HR 97/min, temperature 36.4 C, RR 16/min, BMI >30 kg/m2; labs showed hemoglobin 12.4 g/dL, WBC 10.7 x10^9/L, platelets 304 x10^9/L, glucose 119 mg/dL, creatinine 0.72 mg/dL, and BUN 10.27 mg/dL.

After debridement/fasciotomy and antibiotic failures, deep culture grew Burkholderia cepacia complex susceptible only to meropenem; MRI after meropenem showed phalangeal osteomyelitis, plantar ulcerations, and fistulous pathways; he improved and avoided amputation at one-year follow-up.
